items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Jo Jones was working with Joe Bushkin then.

ctx.x: things would always come to Sherman, you know, and all the bands would come there to play and I'd catch all of them. But anyway, I was with him -- he asked me, says, "How are you going home?" It was hard to get back to New York, Gary. You had to go to Providence and wait a long time and take a bus to Providence and wait and maybe miss a train, then catch a train from Providence to New York. So he was up there, he and his lady, he had his lady and a friend that had driven him there and a Cadillac. He's sitting in…

you know, and lose his money and I'd loan him money, a hundred or something like that because I didn't have any of those habits, see. So he says -- I said, "Well, what the hell. You know if I got anything, you're part of it. Why didn't you?" I says, "You know that." He says, "I know that, but a man's got his pride. You know, a man must have his pride." He says, "I've been down to -- I've called on some others --" I won't call any names "-- that turned me down. I didn't only want like 50 or 75 dollars." He says,…

And he says, "That's who came to my rescue." And I says, "Well, I really didn't know that." And he had left home, he said he couldn't get along, he said, "I can't think no more, I can't practice because I can't get along at home." So he had moved to the Alvin Hotel.
